items.risk: Product breadth and technical relevance do not by themselves establish durable pricing power or market-share capture.
FY GAAP net loss, acquisition integration and normalization of rapid datacenter growth remain material execution variables.
Validation demand can grow while value capture fragments across competing test vendors, integrated equipment diagnostics or customer-built tooling.
Rapid architecture change creates a successor-bottleneck risk: relevance must migrate from current 1.6T products into later optical/electrical interconnect regimes.
GAAP/non-GAAP divergence can inflate perceived operating quality if acquisition amortization, financing and integration costs are treated as economically irrelevant.
Acquisition-related debt and integration can consume cash or management capacity even when current liquidity appears adequate.
AI infrastructure spending may remain strong while VIAVI capture underperforms if customers shift architectures, internalize diagnostics or competitors compress pricing.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong revenue and non-GAAP profitability growth coexist with a FY GAAP net loss.

FY2026 delivered strong revenue growth and positive GAAP operating income while full-year GAAP EPS remained negative; the apparent growth/profitability strength therefore requires reconciliation with below-operating-line and acquisition-related effects.
contradictions.resolution: Beta narrows this from a thesis-invalidating contradiction to an underwriting/accounting-quality question: current evidence shows real operating improvement and adequate year-end liquidity, but does not justify treating non-GAAP profitability as equivalent to distributable earnings. Deep Resolver/Alpha should reconcile the exact FY GAAP loss bridge and organic/acquired contribution.
